Festive Roscón (Sweet Bread Ring)

Served at: Immaculada

Serves 8-10Prep 45 min active, 2-3 hours risingCook 25-35 min

While the most famous Roscón is the Roscón de Reyes for Epiphany, a simpler, festive sweet bread ring, often referred to as a roscón, is a beloved treat enjoyed throughout the holiday period in many Spanish-speaking countries. Immaculada Concepción on December 8th often marks the unofficial start of the Christmas season, making this brioche-like bread, subtly flavored with citrus and adorned with candied fruits, a perfect centerpiece for festive family gatherings.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk, lukewarm
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, divided
  • 3 1/2 cups (420 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon (3 g) salt
  • 2 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1 large egg yolk, at room temperature
  • Zest of 1 large orange
  • Zest of 1/2 lemon
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) orange blossom water (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened and cut into cubes
  • For Decoration:
  • 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) mixed candied fruit, chopped
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) pearl sugar
  • 2 tablespoons (15 g) sliced almonds

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the lukewarm milk, yeast, and 1 teaspoon of the granulated sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, remaining granulated sugar, and salt.
  3. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients. Add the foamy yeast mixture, 2 large eggs, egg yolk, orange zest, lemon zest, and orange blossom water (if using).
  4. Mix with a wooden spoon or a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms. Knead for 5 minutes until it starts to come together.
  5. Gradually add the softened butter, one cube at a time, incorporating each piece before adding the next. Continue kneading for another 10-15 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. It should pass the 'windowpane test' (stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
  6. Form the dough into a ball, place it in a lightly oiled bowl, turn to coat, and cover with plastic wrap or a damp cloth. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. Gently punch down the dough to release the air. On a lightly floured surface, form the dough into a thick rope. Join the ends to form a ring, ensuring the seam is well-sealed. You can also place a small, greased, oven-safe ramekin or ring in the center of a baking sheet to help maintain the hole.
  8. Carefully transfer the dough ring to a parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise again in a warm place for another 45-60 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  9. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
  10. Brush the risen dough gently with the beaten egg wash. Arrange the chopped candied fruit, pearl sugar, and sliced almonds decoratively over the top.
  11. Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until the roscón is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. If it browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with aluminum foil.
  12. Transfer the roscón to a wire rack to cool completely before serving.

Tips

  • Do not rush the rising times; they are crucial for a light and airy texture. A slightly warm, draft-free place is ideal.
  • For extra flavor, you can soak the candied fruits in a tablespoon of rum or orange liqueur for an hour before decorating.
  • Ensure all ingredients, especially eggs and butter, are at room temperature for better incorporation and a smoother dough.
